newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish stocks lose 1.55 percent in correction.
newsitem.headline: Turkish stocks lose 1.55 percent in correction.

text.p: A two-week rally of Turkey's stock market index prompted profit-taking sales on Tuesday.

The IMKB-100 index closed 1,121.37 points or 1.55 percent down at 71,331.54, extending early losses. The index had fallen 0.43 percent in the morning session. It touched the lowest at 70,907 towards the end of the afternoon session.
Total daily volume was 7.89 trillion lira vs 8.07 trillion lira on Monday.
Brokers said Tuesday's decline was a technical correction and was signalled on Monday when the trading volume was low.
The index had gained 11.85 percent in the two-week rally.
"The market did not have sufficient cash inflow at tough resistance levels at 73,000-73,500," said Gokhan Buyuksengur from Sumerbank securities.
He added that the first support levels were expected to be at 69,000-70,000 levels.

"Selling pressure will continue during the week. Unless the index slips well below 70,000 level, the downward movement will continue to be considered as a technical correction," said Murat Emrali from Eczacibasi securities.

Of the 224 shares traded, 137 ended lower, 57 were steady and 30 rose. The 85-share industrial index fell 1.35 percent to 78,208.03 and the 15-share financial index lost 2.03 percent to close at 63,283.57.
Utility firms led the active shares. Cukurova Elektrik kept steady. Aktas Elektrik was also unchanged at 53,000.
